input_references.role: Timestamped GPS points linked to each selected taxi request
Locations and region labels for the fixed taxi stands

metadata.goal: Analyze recurring patterns and longer-term changes in taxi demand across the city.
metadata.category: Citywide demand periodicity, peak spatial structure, and longitudinal change
metadata.header: Recurring Taxi Demand and Peak Sources
metadata.dataset_description: A Porto Taxi case containing 715 taxi requests from six widely spaced observation dates. The demand table records request time, peak period, pickup and dropoff locations, request source, and taxi-stand identity; linked GPS points provide each trip trajectory; the stand table provides stand locations and regions.

insight_list.insight: Citywide taxi demand follows a recurring low–high–low–high–low daily cycle, with a morning peak, a midday lull, a larger late-afternoon peak, and low demand overnight and late at night.

plot.title: Recurring Citywide Taxi Demand Cycle
plot.description: Thin lines show the five-period demand profile for each observation date; the blue line is the cross-date mean.

insight_list.question: What recurring within-day pattern does citywide taxi demand exhibit across the supplied observation dates?

insight_list.insight: The two daily peaks have different spatial structures: morning-peak demand is broadly distributed across the western and eastern suburban service areas, whereas late-afternoon demand is densely concentrated in Porto's central district.

plot.title: Spatial Structure of the Two Daily Demand Peaks
plot.description: Pickup locations and their linked trip trajectories contrast the broad suburban morning peak with the compact central late-afternoon peak.

insight_list.question: How do the spatial distributions of taxi requests and linked trajectories differ between the morning and late-afternoon demand peaks?

insight_list.insight: The low–high–low–high–low cycle recurs across all observation dates, but the two daily peak totals fluctuate while trending upward over the longer observation period.

plot.title: Peak Demand Across Observation Dates
plot.description: The morning and late-afternoon peak totals are shown for six widely spaced observation dates.

insight_list.question: Does the recurring daily cycle remain stable across the longer observation period, and how do the two peak totals change across dates?

insight_list.insight: Over the longer observation period, morning-peak growth comes from two fixed stands, whereas late-afternoon growth comes from two different fixed stands.

plot.title: Peak Growth from Designated Stands versus All Other Stands
plot.description: Each panel compares the two growing stands, the combined total of every other observed stand, and total peak demand. The combined comparison group remains flat.

insight_list.question: After comparing the designated stands with the combined total of all other observed stands, which fixed stands account for each peak's growth, and do the growing morning and late-afternoon stands overlap?

insight_value.evidence: Morning-peak growth comes from the fixed Matosinhos Edge and Campanhã Outer suburban stands, while the other observed morning stands remain flat; late-afternoon growth comes from the fixed Aliados and São Bento central stands, while its other observed stands remain flat.

insights: Citywide taxi demand follows a recurring low–high–low–high–low daily cycle, with a morning peak, a midday lull, a larger late-afternoon peak, and low demand overnight and late at night.

The two daily peaks have different spatial structures: morning-peak demand is broadly distributed across the western and eastern suburban service areas, whereas late-afternoon demand is densely concentrated in Porto's central district.
The low–high–low–high–low cycle recurs across all observation dates, but the two daily peak totals fluctuate while trending upward over the longer observation period.
Over the longer observation period, morning-peak growth comes from two fixed stands, whereas late-afternoon growth comes from two different fixed stands.
summary: Taxi demand repeatedly follows a low–high–low–high–low daily cycle across the six supplied dates. The morning and late-afternoon peaks have contrasting spatial structures—broad suburban demand in the morning and compact central demand later in the day—and both peak totals fluctuate but rise over time. Their growth comes from distinct, fixed groups of suburban versus central taxi stands.
